title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context (pp. 5-7): Grothendieck is building a combinatorial 'analysis situs' of 'figures'. A figure F is a finite stratified subset |F| = sup F = ∪ X_i of an ambient space T. Each X_i is a closed stratum in Σ_F, with open stratum int(X_i) = U_i = X_i minus ∂X_i, and the closed strata are the closures of the open ones. For a closed stratum X, F_X is the induced sub-figure. A subset A of |F| is F-saturated if it is a union of open strata. The page sets up a 'compatibility' relation between two figures F and F'. A crossed-out first attempt (c) tried to define it via a common sub-figure F''. The page then compares two conditions. (a), from p.5: for all X in Σ_F and X' in Σ_F', the intersection X ∩ X' is both F_X-saturated and F'_X'-saturated. (b): for any connected open stratum U_i of F and U'_j of F', either U_i ∩ U'_j = ∅ or U_i = U'_j. Claim: (a) and (b) are equivalent. (b)⇒(a) is called trivial. Indeed, if U_i ⊂ X meets X', it meets some U'_j ⊂ X', hence equals it, so X ∩ X' is a union of strata of F_X, and symmetrically. (a)⇒(b): pick x in U_i ∩ U'_j. X_i ∩ X'_j is closed and F_{X_i}-saturated and contains x in U_i. So it contains U_i, hence its closure X_i, giving X_i ⊂ X'_j. By symmetry X'_j ⊂ X_i, so X_i = X'_j. It remains to show ∂X_i = ∂X'_j, which yields U_i = U'_j. Grothendieck does this by induction on sup(dim F, dim F'), passing to the figures F_{X_i} and F'_{X'_j} (their boundaries have lower dimension). Page 7 then calls F and F' 'compatible' if these conditions hold. It notes that this reduces to compatibility of elementary figures. It defines a 'configuration' as a set of pairwise compatible figures. This is essentially the face-to-face intersection axiom of polyhedral or regular cell complexes, set up axiomatically for a tame-topology framework.
errors: The step 'X_i ∩ X'_j saturated and containing x in U_i implies U_i ⊂ X_i ∩ X'_j' uses saturation for the stratification of F_{X_i}. It also needs U_i to be a single (connected) stratum and X_i to be the closure of U_i. This is a regularity assumption on figures that is implicit here.

The final step U_i = U'_j (equivalently ∂X_i = ∂X'_j) is only sketched via induction on dimension. One must check that (a) for F, F' implies (a) for the boundary figures F_{∂X_i} and F'_{∂X'_j}. This is plausible (closed strata of the boundary are closed strata of F) but not written.
Minor: the crossed-out draft states the wrong direction as trivial before correcting it to 'b) ⇒ a) trivial'.

ideas.what: Compatibility of two stratified 'figures': closed strata intersect in saturated subsets, equivalently open connected strata are disjoint or equal
ideas.modern_name: Face-to-face (proper) intersection condition for polyhedral/regular CW complexes; compatible stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology / polyhedral geometry (simplicial complexes, Whitehead, Zeeman, etc.)
ideas.where_published: Only the general program of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this specific formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Configuration = set of pairwise compatible figures (elementary figures)
ideas.modern_name: Polyhedral complex / cell complex as a set of cells closed under faces with pairwise proper intersection

ideas.what: Proof technique: induction on dimension via the induced figures F_X on closed strata
ideas.modern_name: Standard induction over the skeleton/strata of a regular stratification

deep.surprise_reason: A routine foundational lemma in an axiomatic setup of stratified 'figures'. Its content is the classical face-to-face condition of cell complexes. It is interesting only as documentation of how Grothendieck began formalising tame topology in 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'a $U_i \cap U'_j = \emptyset$ ou $U_i = U'_j$' : the leading 'a' is 'on a' (i.e. 'alors on a ...').
'Les conditions [?] sont équivalentes' likely reads 'Ces conditions [a) et b)] sont équivalentes'.
Line 'il suffit [?] ... $x \in U_i \cap U'_j$' is better read as 'Soit $x \in U_i \cap U'_j$, considérons $X_i \cap X'_j$'.

'On en peut en conclure aussitôt [?] directement' is closer to 'On ne peut en conclure aussi directement $\partial X_i = \partial X'_j$', i.e. the boundary equality is not immediate. Hence the induction on sup(dim F, dim F').
